evals.prompt: The red backpack shows up in eight of our illustrations. Make sure it looks the same in all of them.
evals.expected_output: The agent writes a frozen identity paragraph with proportions, counts, material, vivid colour names and marks, renders three master takes in the project's style on a flat background, lets the user pick, renders each angle from the master with the fixed references role and a geometric frame.view sentence in a JSON prompt, checks one sheet, and saves prop.json.
assertions: Writes the identity paragraph before rendering, with proportions, counts, material, colour names, and marks
Sends every render as a JSON specification built from the style file, not a prose prompt
Renders the master alone, three-quarter view, flat plain background, no cast shadow, 3 takes, and lets the user pick
Attaches the master to every angle render with a references role that keeps identity and ignores pose
Sets frame.view to a geometric angle sentence rather than just a name
Uses the identity paragraph verbatim as subject.object in every prompt
Builds one sheet of master and angles and compares each with the master before asking for approval
Saves prop.json with the identity paragraph, style, model, angles map, and job ids

evals.prompt: The side view of the kettle keeps coming out three-quarter. Can you just warp it in an editor?
evals.expected_output: The agent does not pixel-edit. It re-renders the side angle with the master plus a second image whose role is pose only, and checks it against the master.
assertions: Does not warp or pixel-edit the render
Adds a second reference whose references role is 'pose reference only: take nothing from it but the pose'
Compares the new render with the master on a sheet

evals.prompt: We have the violet lunchbox as a prop. Now I need a pink one and an open one.
evals.expected_output: The agent attaches the master and states only what changes for each variant, then renders and checks the variant's angles like any prop.
assertions: Attaches the existing master for each variant
States only the change in subject.object, such as 'Only the body colour changes, from violet to pink.'
Keeps the rest of the identity paragraph verbatim
Sends each variant render as a JSON specification
Checks the variant renders on a sheet against the master
